items.title: docs(mcpx): the FAQ and a runnable examples gallery (#1859)
items.body: Closes #1859 (parent #94; triage task 2747 verdict CONFIRMED). ## What this adds **`pkgs/mcpx/docs/faq.md`** — the level-2 FAQ. The five questions from the notes are headings word for word (quotes, `, no.` and `..` included), each with its fixed anchor set explicitly (``, the form that works on GitHub now and in mdBook later, as the page map requires): `faq#do-you-like-mcp`, `faq#opencode-code-mode`, `faq#is-it-safe`, `faq#why`, `faq#examples`. Each answer is ~120 words, in the notes' own "we" voice, and ends with exactly one "more" link into a page that exists today (`story.md`, `opencode-plugin.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `ASSESSMENT.md`, `examples.md`). Facts, and where they come from: - MCP versus the one mcpx made: `docs/story.md` "Summary" and "mcpx speaks MCP". - Code mode: the `OPENCODE-V2.md` **correction block** and `docs/opencode-plugin.md` §1 — v1 ships it behind `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE`, both accept TypeScript — never the stale body. `OPENCODE-V2.md` itself is untouched; it belongs to the compendium tracker. - Safety: `AGENTS.md` "Scripts" (this is the citation that replaces the issue's drifted `internal/runner/runner.go:41-66`), plus the daemon's unauthenticated loopback/socket posture from `docs/story.md` "One daemon, many clients". "Is it safe?" starts with **No.** and describes the posture; it designs no security. - Why: `ASSESSMENT.md` and the opening walk. - Examples: points at the gallery below. **`pkgs/mcpx/examples/`** — four runnable scripts and the test that runs them, Approach C of the issue: | example | shows | | --- | --- | | `call-a-tool.ts` | the whole shape: top-level `await`, one argument object, print the result | | `discover.ts` | `Object.keys(tools.demo)`, `describe()`, then two calls in one script | | `stateful.ts` | `open` then `state` in one invocation, and `log()` | | `recipe-echo.ts` | a real `// @param` recipe, saved and run through `mcpx recipes` | `examples_test.go` builds the CLI and the `fakemcp` fixture through `internal/testsupport`, gives each run its own `HOME`, `MCPX_STATE_DIR`, `MCPX_CACHE_DIR` and `MCPX_CONFIG`, sets `MCPX_AUTOSTART_IDLE_EXIT=60s`, and runs `mcpx stop --all` on cleanup — the daemon-hygiene pattern from `internal/e2e` (#52/#182). Each script is run from a temp copy (so `mcpx run`'s generated `mcpx-client.ts` never lands in the tree) and its stdout is compared with a checked-in `.expected.txt`, with a line diff on failure. Deterministic: the fixture server only, no Chrome, no network, no clock. Because it is a Go test in `pkgs/mcpx`, the existing `mcpx` workflow's `go test ./...` executes it — no new workflow, and an example that rots fails the build. **`pkgs/mcpx/docs/examples.md`** — the gallery, derived from those files: per example the script, the command, and the exact stdout. `faq#examples` links to it. Every fenced block was checked against the `.ts` and `.expected.txt` bytes. ## Two small corrections the directory forces - `internal/defaults/links_test.go`: a backticked path that is not at the module root is now also tried against the citing document. The plugin skills write `examples/README.md` and mean the directory beside `SKILL.md`; before, those were skipped only because no top-level `examples/` existed. `examples/servers/` joins `foreignPrefixes` — it is the cloned official conformance suite's layout, the same category as `docs/extensions/`. - `plugin/opencode/README.md` named `examples/screenshot-and-errors.ts` for the browser skill's example; it names the real path now. ## Verification ``` go test ./examples/ -count=1 → ok (TestExamples, 4/4 subtests PASS) go test ./internal/defaults/ -count=1 → ok (TestEveryDocumentationLinkResolves) go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1 → ok (docs guards, story quote/line counts) gofmt -l examples internal/defaults → empty ``` Not run locally: the full `go test ./...` (CI's job) and `nix build` (not triggered by a docs-only change). ## Not in this PR - No links added from the home page or "now what": neither page exists yet (#1874, #1878). The link targets are already the fixed `faq#…` anchors, so those pages can point at them when they land. - `docs/scripts.md` (the other back-link the issue names) is #2108's page; the FAQ links to `AGENTS.md` instead of a page that is not there. - `OPENCODE-V2.md`'s stale body is left to the compendium tracker, per the issue's exclusion. Its correction block is what the FAQ cites. Queue task: 3069 (worker `repo-worker-code`, OpenChamber scheduled lane). --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(openclaw): opencode-route provider proxy — OpenCode server front for OpenClaw (#2229)
items.body: Method 3 of code#2229: an OpenAI-compatible front so OpenClaw can run jobs carried by the OpenCode workhorse route. ## What - **bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs** (new): chat-completions facade on fixed port **18750** (next free in the #437 block), mirroring the commandcode proxy pattern. Each request creates one session on the laptop OpenCode server via its v2 API (`POST /api/session` with `model:{providerID:"opencode-route", id:}`), prompts it, waits for settle, and returns the assistant text as a chat completion. Streaming supported via message polling. OpenAI tool_calls are not round-tripped — the OpenCode build agent executes with its own tools server-side (documented in the file header). - **bin/opencode-route-proxy-start.sh** + **bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs** (new; tests pass 2/2). - **home/common/default.nix**: `opencodeRouteProxyPort = 18750`, proxy-supervisor entry, manual-fallback systemd unit (no Install.WantedBy — the supervisor owns the process, per the 2026-10-26 commandcode lesson). - **home/openclaw/default.nix**: `models.providers.opencode-route` (workhorse, speed, specialist, summit, scout), gateway After/Wants on the proxy unit, laptop-operations port list updated. ## Live proof (2026-10-29, from this worktree) - `POST /v1/chat/completions {model:"opencode-route/workhorse"}` → `ROUTE-PROXY-OK`. - `openclaw agent --local --model opencode-route/workhorse` → replied **OC-ROUTE-OK**; run meta: provider `opencode-route`, model `workhorse`, fallbackUsed=false. - Verified in the OpenCode v2 tables: session **ses_e5e78b6f4f4ffeVyPSZquFZkwV** ("opencode-route-proxy: workhorse"), assistant carried by providerID `opencode-go`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, variant `high` — the workhorse pool door. Deploys permanently at the next switch (supervisor takes over port 18750 from the checkout). --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint for health checks, model listings, and chat completions. * Added five selectable OpenCode models: Workhorse, Speed, Specialist, Summit, and Scout. * Chat completions support both streaming and non-streaming responses, with usage information included for streaming. * The service restarts automatically if it stops, and completion requests have a configurable timeout. * **Bug Fixes** * Invalid or empty requests and unavailable upstream services now return clear error responses.
